n: In this lecture we talk about natural phenylalkylamines: ephedrine, mescaline, cathine and cathinone, their narcological significance and methods of analysis. The outline is as follows: classification, plant sources, that is, khat, ephedra and peyote, then ephedrine and ephedrone, mescaline, isolation, colour reactions and physico-chemical methods. Key terms: amphetamine derivatives, ephedrine, ephedrone, cathine, cathinone, mescaline, Reinecke salt and ninhydrin.

Phenylalkylamines form the basis of most synthetic narcotic drugs and are referred to as amphetamine derivatives. On the illicit market, more than 20 substances of this group are in circulation. Its first representatives were obtained from various plants. Later, to increase narcotic properties and potency, many semi-synthetic and synthetic derivatives were synthesised, numbering more than a hundred. There are three synthetic classes.

Phenylalkylamines are conventionally divided into natural and synthetic groups, and the synthetic derivatives are divided into 3 classes. The classes consist of derivatives with substitution of the hydrogen of the amino group, of the alkyl group and of the benzene ring. The table shows benzene ring derivatives: in the monomethoxy group PMA, PMMA, 4-MTA; in the dimethoxy group DOM, DOET, DOX, DOB; in the methylenedioxy group MDA, MDMA, MBDB, BDB, MDMMA; in the trimethoxy group mescaline. Remember: the classification is conventional, and substances cannot be strictly divided into groups.

In the scheme, let us look at the classification once more. Phenylalkylamines are conventionally divided into natural and synthetic groups, and synthetic derivatives are divided into 3 classes. In the first class the hydrogen of the amino group is substituted, in the second that of the alkyl group, in the third that of the benzene ring. The natural representatives have been identified in khat, ephedra herb and the peyote cactus: khat contains cathinone and cathine, ephedra ephedrine, peyote mescaline.

Let us compare the three plants. Khat grows in East Africa and on the Arabian Peninsula and is known as “Arabian tea”. Ephedra grows in the mountainous regions of Central Asia and was used in China for 5000 years. Mescaline was isolated from the peyote cactus in 1896, and the powder from its flowers contains up to 8% mescaline. The main substance in khat is cathinone and cathine, in ephedra ephedrine, in peyote mescaline.

The first representatives of the phenylalkylamines were identified in three plants: khat, in Latin Catha edulis, ephedra herb, Herba Ephedrae, and the peyote cactus, Lophophora williamsii. As the table shows, the main substances are cathinone and cathine in khat, ephedrine and pseudoephedrine in ephedra herb, and mescaline in the peyote cactus.

Khat, Catha edulis, grows in East Africa and on the Arabian Peninsula. Its dried leaves are known as “Arabian tea” and are consumed by the local population. The leaves contain the alkaloids cathinone and cathine. The content of the active components is from 0.5 to 2%.

An important aspect connected with khat is storage. During drying, the alkaloid cathinone, a psychostimulant, evaporates. For this reason the leaves are distributed in plastic containers or wrapped in banana leaves. Besides alkaloids, the plant contains cathidine, cathinine, choline, bromides, fatty acids, essential oils and other alkaloids.

Ephedra is a low shrub-like plant with a much-branched, green, flexible stem. It grows in the mountainous regions of Central Asia. It contains the alkaloids ephedrine and pseudoephedrine, tannins and pyrocatechol, but only ephedrine is of significance. In China, wild ephedra was used for 5000 years for malaria, cough and to improve work capacity.

In folk medicine, an ephedra infusion is used for rheumatism and diseases of the gastrointestinal tract and respiratory tract. Under the action of the plant, the excitability of the central nervous system increases, blood vessels constrict and blood pressure rises. The smooth muscles of the bronchi relax, urine and sweat excretion increases, and body temperature falls. In other words, the action concerns not only the nervous system but several organs and systems.

The main active substance of the ephedra plant is the alkaloid ephedrine. Its stereoisomer pseudoephedrine occurs in the ephedra plant and can also be obtained synthetically. Ephedrine as the base dissolves well in ethyl alcohol, ether and chloroform, while its hydrochloride dissolves well in water and alcohol. In medicine ephedrine is used as the hydrochloride in tablets, solution and drops, and it is also a component of theophedrine.

Ephedrine has an adrenaline-like action and is used in bronchial asthma and eye diseases. It raises arterial blood pressure, constricts vessels, dilates the bronchi and the pupil, and stimulates the central nervous system. It is absorbed rapidly: 80% of the dose taken is excreted unchanged in urine within a day. It has a relaxing effect on the nervous system and causes delirium and, in part, euphoria.

Ephedrine and its oxidation product ephedrone are excreted in urine, so the main specimen is urine. The urine is made alkaline to pH=10 with a 10% solution of potassium carbonate. Then it is extracted with chloroform. Reactions and thin-layer chromatography are carried out on the resulting chloroform extract.

Ephedrone causes strong euphoria. Its specimens are the urine of toxicomaniacs and the liquids they have consumed. Ephedrine is oxidised with potassium permanganate and acetic acid at 50-60 °C to form ephedrone. This liquid is consumed for euphoria. Thus ephedrone arises from the oxidation of ephedrine.

t: Effect of ephedrone on the body
n: The effect of ephedrone on the body is as follows. Tachycardia and mydriasis, that is, dilation of the pupil, are observed. Dry skin, raised blood pressure, arrhythmia and loss of consciousness also occur. Remember: ephedrone rapidly causes dependence.

t: Ephedrine: Dragendorff and copper salt reactions
n: Reactions for detecting ephedrine. With Dragendorff reagent, ephedrine forms dark red needle-shaped crystals. In a micro-test tube, 1-2 drops of solution are acidified with acetic acid, a 5% solution of copper sulphate is added, and an alkaline medium is created with ammonia. Then 2 drops of a 1:3 mixture of CS2 and benzene are added and shaken, and the benzene layer is coloured yellow or brown.

The reaction with Reinecke salt is carried out microcrystalloscopically. On a slide, a freshly prepared 1% solution of Reinecke salt is dropped onto the residue of 1-2 drops of solution. After 5-10 minutes, under the microscope, clusters of four-sided reddish-pink crystals are seen for ephedrine. Ephedrone, in turn, forms clusters of thin straight-edged crystals with Reinecke salt.

In thin-layer chromatography the system is chloroform and acetone 48:2, and the visualising reagent is a solution of ninhydrin in acetone. On the plate Rf=0.28 for ephedrine and Rf=0.71 for ephedrone. Another system is also used: chloroform:acetone 9:1. In it, with ninhydrin, ink-coloured spots form on a pink background.

Spectral features of ephedrine. Its acidic solution absorbs maximally in the UV spectrum at 251, 257 and 263 nm. In the IR spectrum, in a KBr pellet, absorption bands are observed at 994, 699, 754, 1242 and 670 cm-1. The amount of ephedrine is found in UV spectrophotometry from the graph of absorbance against concentration.

We compare the mass spectra. In the mass spectrum of ephedrine the main peaks are 58, 146, 56, 105, 77, 42, 106 and 40 m/z. In the mass spectrum of ephedrone they are 58, 77, 51, 56, 42, 105, 50 and 43 m/z. For both substances 58 m/z is in first place, and the remaining peaks differ in order.

Qualitative reactions of ephedrone. With Dragendorff reagent, ephedrone also forms dark red needle-shaped crystals. With an alkaline solution of copper (II) sulphate and a solution of CS2 in benzene, a dithiocarbamic acid derivative is formed, and the benzene layer is coloured yellow-brown. With Reinecke salt, clusters of thin straight-edged crystals are formed.

UV and IR spectra of ephedrone. A solution of ephedrone in 0.1 M HCl absorbs maximally at 251 nm, and in 0.1 M alkali at 247 nm. If ephedrone as the base is dissolved in 0.1 M sulphuric acid, maxima at 251, 257 and 263 nm form in the spectrum. In the IR spectrum, in a KBr disc, absorption bands at 1691, 705, 1245 and 1469 cm-1 are seen.

There are two methods of determining ephedrone quantitatively. The absorbance of the coloured complex formed with copper salts and CS2 is determined by the photoelectrocolorimetry (PEC) method. The amount can also be found by calculation after determining the absorbance of a solution of ephedrone in hydrochloric acid.

Ephedrine and ephedrone can be distinguished. Dragendorff reagent gives needle-shaped crystals for both substances, and the difference appears with Reinecke salt and in TLC. With Reinecke salt, ephedrine forms four-sided crystals and ephedrone thin straight-edged crystals. In TLC, ephedrone, Rf=0.71, rises higher than ephedrine, Rf=0.28. The UV spectrum of ephedrone in 0.1 M HCl gives a maximum only at 251 nm.

Now we turn to the peyote cactus. The Indians of South America used cacti containing mescaline in religious ceremonies, and infusions were prepared from peyote. The hallucinogenic alkaloid mescaline was first isolated in 1896 from Lophophora williamsii. The flowers contain a lot of mescaline. On the illicit market, dry ground flower powder is distributed in gelatin capsules, and it contains up to 8% mescaline.

Action of mescaline. Mescaline in an amount of 200-500 mg, as the hydrochloride or sulphate, has a hallucinogenic effect. The effect of a single dose is observed for 12 hours. The action begins 30-60 minutes after intake and lasts 4-6 hours. Pure mescaline is a colourless dry crystalline substance, 4000 times weaker than LSD.

Toxic dose and metabolism of mescaline. At 5-10 mg/kg, tremor, nausea, headache, agitation, hallucinations and suicidal impulses are observed. At 20 mg/kg, paralysis of the central nervous system and respiratory centre may occur with death. In metabolism, mescaline is acetylated to form N-acetylmescaline, hydroxylated, and by deamination 3,4,5-trimethoxyacetic and 3,4,5-trimethoxybenzoic acids are formed.

The general scheme of phenylalkylamine analysis. First the substances are isolated: with acidified water or alcohol, then the aqueous extract is extracted 3 times with chloroform at pH=9-12. Preliminary reactions: Marquis reagent gives an orange colour, ninhydrin violet. For confirmation, TLC, UV and IR spectrometry and mass spectrometry are used.

Ephedrine, ephedrone, cathine, cathinone and mescaline are isolated from biological specimens by the acidified water or alcohol method. The aqueous extracts are brought to pH=9-12 and extracted three times with chloroform. The chloroform layer is passed through a filter with anhydrous sodium sulphate and evaporated to 0.5-1 ml.

The procedure for extraction from biological fluids. 10 ml of blood or 50 ml of urine is brought to pH=10-11 with 25% ammonia solution. Then it is extracted 3 times with a 9:1 mixture of chloroform and n-butanol. The organic layer is passed through 1 g of anhydrous Na2SO4, 100 µl of 5% HCl is added, and it is evaporated to 0.5-1.0 ml.

In chemical analysis two reagents occupy the main place. With Marquis reagent, phenylalkylamines give an orange colour. With ninhydrin solution a violet colour forms. In TLC the system is chloroform-acetone-ethanol-ammonia 25% in the ratio 20:3:1:20, the visualising reagent is ninhydrin, and Rf=0.36 for phenylalkylamines.

The colours with Marquis reagent are given in the table. A 5-10 mg tablet is ground in a mortar and tested in a porcelain dish with 2-3 drops of Marquis reagent. MDA, MDMA, MDEA, MBDB and BDB give a bluish-black, that is, green-black colour. Mescaline gives orange, methamphetamine brown, DOM/STP yellow. According to the table, PMA gives light grey and DOB emerald green.

Rf values in TLC depend on the plate. The system chloroform-acetone-ethanol-ammonia 25% in the ratio 20:3:1:20 is used, with Merck and Sorbfil plates. On the Sorbfil plate the values are higher: for example, for MDA 0.44 and 0.66, for MDMA 0.12 and 0.23, for mescaline 0.36 and 0.50. The colours with Marquis reagent and ninhydrin are evaluated together with Rf.

UV absorption maxima are determined in 0.1 M HCl. Amphetamine, methamphetamine, ephedrine and norpseudoephedrine give maxima at 251, 257 and 263 nm. Ephedrone gives a maximum at 251 nm, MDA and MDMA at 235 and 286 nm. N-ethyl-MDA and MBDB give maxima at 234 and 286 nm.

Preliminary analysis of DOB, DOX or DOM. The filter paper containing the substance is cut into 1x1 cm pieces, and 1 ml of chloroform and 1 drop of 0.1 M KOH are added. The solution is boiled on a water bath, and after cooling the organic layer is separated and evaporated to dryness. When 2-3 drops of Marquis reagent are added to the residue, a colour appears.

Mescaline appears in TLC as follows. On the Merck plate Rf=0.36, on the Sorbfil plate Rf=0.50. With Marquis reagent mescaline gives orange, with ninhydrin violet. System: chloroform-acetone-ethanol-25% ammonia solution, in the ratio 20:3:1:20.

We look at the connection with precursors. The list of precursors names ephedrine, pseudoephedrine, norpseudoephedrine, N-methylephedrine and phenylpropanolamine. Ephedrine and N-methylephedrine are listed for obtaining methcathinone, norpseudoephedrine for norcathinone, and phenylpropanolamine for cathinone and methcathinone. Pseudoephedrine is linked with pervitin. Potassium permanganate is also given in the list as a precursor for obtaining methcathinone.

To conclude. The natural phenylalkylamines are the alkaloids of khat, ephedra and peyote: khat cathine and cathinone, ephedra ephedrine, peyote mescaline. Ephedrine and ephedrone are extracted from urine into chloroform with K2CO3 at pH 10, then identified with Dragendorff and Reinecke reagents, the Cu-CS2 reaction, TLC, and UV, IR and MS. Review questions: structure of ephedrine; obtaining and quantitative analysis of ephedrone; distinguishing ephedrine and ephedrone; from which plants phenylalkylamines are obtained.
